claims.text: Reliable formation of noble metal–based HEA nanomaterials is governed by the degree of atomic-level mixing and elemental uniformity achieved during synthesis.
Greater elemental homogeneity improves catalytic activity.
Greater elemental homogeneity improves catalytic stability.
Synergistic electronic effects mediate the performance benefit of greater elemental homogeneity.
Greater elemental homogeneity suppresses phase segregation.
Rapid quenching, optimized precursor ratios, or high-temperature synthesis can produce nanoparticles with higher atomic-level mixing.
Slower cooling, suboptimal precursor ratios, or lower synthesis temperature can produce nanoparticles with lower atomic-level mixing.
The comparison will test both nanoparticle sets under the same reaction, temperature, solvent, and substrate concentration.
STEM-EDS mapping or atom probe tomography can characterize the degree of atomic-level mixing and uniformity.
Homogeneous mixing enables synergistic electronic interactions among constituent metals.
Synergistic electronic interactions optimize catalytic active sites.
Prevention of phase segregation enhances catalytic activity and stability.
Nanoparticles with higher atomic-level mixing will have at least twofold greater catalytic activity than lower-mixing nanoparticles.
Nanoparticles with higher atomic-level mixing will show measurably greater resistance to deactivation or metal leaching than lower-mixing nanoparticles.
The proposed relationship applies to noble metal–based HEA nanoparticles in reactions where synergistic effects are relevant, including oxidation and hydrogenation.
The proposed relationship may not apply to non-noble-metal HEAs or bulk alloys.
The magnitude of catalytic improvement depends on the particular constituent metals and reaction conditions.
Phase segregation may not be detrimental for every composition or reaction.
If the higher-mixing nanoparticles do not show significantly greater activity and stability than the lower-mixing nanoparticles, the hypothesis is falsified.
